notes: Built from the PDF text only (pdftotext -layout). The download is a single clean copy (19 pages, no redline); position statements were 'maintained' at the 09/15/25 revision.
Dates: effective_date is the 'Revised: 09/15/25' date of this version; the original effective date is 02/15/01; reviewed 08/28/25 (committee approval 08/28/25).

Plan types: the header says the guideline applies to all lines of business unless noted in Program Exceptions. FEP and SAO follow their own guidelines; Medicare Advantage follows NCD 240.4 and DMERC LCDs L33718 / L33800.

Code-to-pathway mapping. E0601: adult initial, pediatric initial, continued coverage for OSA, re-qualification, replacement. E0470: bi-level OSA initial, restrictive thoracic, severe COPD (E0470), COPD hospital discharge, central sleep apnea, hypoventilation (E0470), continued coverage for OSA, continued coverage non-OSA, re-qualification, replacement. E0471: restrictive thoracic, severe COPD after E0470 (criterion I), COPD hospital discharge (criterion II), central sleep apnea, hypoventilation (E0471), continued coverage non-OSA, replacement. E0561/E0562: humidifier pathway, plus the pediatric initial pathway because that sentence names them. A-codes and S8186: accessories pathway. A7047, A7049, E0530, E0600, A7002: investigational, no pathway.

Each section names its own HCPCS codes, so no code had to be mapped by inference. The replacement pathway's 'PAP device' is read as the three devices E0601, E0470, E0471; the re-qualification sentence's 'PAP device' as the two OSA devices E0601, E0470 (the initial 3-month PAP trial it refers to is the OSA trial).

E0600 and A7002 appear only in a billing NOTE ('may sometimes be reported' for oral pressure therapy, which is investigational); they are tagged investigational to match the document's own tagging of the OPT interface A7047 as Investigational. A reviewer could omit them because the codes describe a generic suction pump. E0465/E0466/E0467 (ventilators) are left to policy 09-E0000-55 and omitted.

E0471 is tagged covered in scope.cpt because four pathways grant it (restrictive thoracic, COPD, CSA, hypoventilation). The statements that E0471 does not meet medical necessity for OSA (position statement and billing NOTE with the OSA ICD-10 codes) are exclusions with an empty cpt list, since the code is not wholly that excluded thing; a check of E0471 for an OSA diagnosis would fail every pathway that names E0471 (none is an OSA pathway).

Device/population/phase split: one pathway per device code group and per section as printed. Restrictive thoracic and CSA grant 'E0470 or E0471' with one set of criteria, so each is one pathway with both codes rather than two identical pathways.

Adult initial: the sentence 'AHI... of 5 or more but less than 15 in adult members with symptomatic OSA (...)' holds two requirements (the index range and symptomatic adult OSA) and is split into two criteria under an 'all'; the 15-or-more alternative is one criterion. Threshold for the 5-to-15 criterion is gte 5 only (a value of 15 or more satisfies the other branch).

Pediatric initial: the NOTE 'In pediatric members, an AHI or RDI greater than or equal to 1.0 is considered abnormal' is placed in the pediatric pathway as the sleep-test threshold a child must show. A reviewer could treat it as definitional and leave it out. The third bullet 'adenotonsillectomy has been unsuccessful or is contraindicated, or when definitive surgery is indicated but must wait...' is an 'any' of two criteria (the first keeps 'unsuccessful or is contraindicated' together as one either/or about the same surgery).

Bi-level for OSA (E0470): the section itself states only 'CPAP has been tried and proven ineffective or is not tolerated'. The OSA diagnostic block (sleep test, report with index, AHI thresholds) is nested in because the switching paragraphs require 'the above criteria' / 'the criteria above' to be met when substituting bi-level. The switch timing is an 'any': found ineffective during the initial 3-month home trial (no new evaluation or sleep test) OR CPAP used more than 3 months and a new initial face-to-face clinical evaluation. A CPAP failure during an in-lab titration fits neither paragraph literally and would read as insufficient on that 'any'; a reviewer could instead model it as not(used more than 3 months) OR new evaluation.

'A new 3-month trial would begin for use of bi-level therapy or APAP' is informational (resets the initial phase) and is not a criterion. A switch from CPAP to APAP stays under E0601; its new-evaluation rule is a conditional in the adult initial pathway (second check).

NOTE after the switching paragraphs ('If the above criteria are not met, continued coverage of a PAP device and related accessories will be denied') and the matching sentences under the E0470/E0471 hypoventilation criteria, the continued-coverage section and the accessories paragraph are the contrapositive of their pathways; they are not listed as exclusions.

Re-qualification: 'A member who fails (including member non-adherence) the initial 3-month PAP trial is eligible to re-qualify ... but must have a face-to-face clinical re-evaluation' is its own pathway (failure + re-evaluation + the OSA diagnostic block, since 're-qualify' means meeting the qualifying criteria again). The PDF prints 'f ace-to-face' with a kerning gap; the criterion text uses 'face-to-face'.

Restrictive thoracic: 'One of the following' a/b/c is an 'any'; c holds a condition (progressive neuromuscular disease only) and two alternatives (MIP less than 60 cm H2O, FVC less than 50% predicted), modeled as all[condition, any[MIP, FVC]]. 'H20' is kept as printed in the criterion text. The disorder-group list ('clinical disorder groups characterized as one of the following') is modeled as a diagnosis leaf at the top of each disorder pathway (restrictive thoracic disorder, severe COPD, hypoventilation syndrome; for CSA the diagnosis is already criterion 1).

Severe COPD E0470: A, B and C are all required (the list reads 'A ...; B ...; AND C'). The E0471 sentence 'meets the definition of medical necessity for either criterion I or II' is split into two pathways: I (after initial E0470 use, A and B) for E0471 only, and II (started at hospital discharge, up to 3 months) for both E0470 and E0471 because the sentence names '(E0470, E0471)'. 'For members with COPD who qualified for an E0470 device' is a single leaf rather than a nested copy of the E0470 criteria. Criterion I.A 'PaCO2 greater than 52 or pre ABG PaCO2 increase equal to or greater than 7 mm HG' is an 'any' of two criteria.

Central sleep apnea: the facility-based attended polysomnogram is its own leaf and the three things it must document are leaves under one 'all'. Criterion 2 is conditional ('if either CSA or OSA is a component of the initially observed sleep-associated hypoventilation'); kept as one leaf with the condition in the question. The ASV / CHF NOTE (LVEF <= 45%) is an exclusion with no code because E0471 is also granted for CSA when LVEF is above 45%; the sentence allowing ASV at clinical discretion for LVEF > 45% or mild CHF-related CSA is not a criterion.

Hypoventilation: 'A, B AND either criterion C or D' = all[A, B, any[C, D]] for each of E0470 and E0471. 'Spirometry shows an FEV1/FVC greater than or equal to 70%' is printed identically in both and is one shared criterion; the ABG and PSG criteria differ in wording between the two sections and are separate criteria. The parenthetical referral to SEVERE COPD for FEV1/FVC below 70% is a cross-reference, not a requirement.

Continued coverage for OSA (E0601, E0470): adherence must be documented between day 31 and day 91; the adherence definition holds two numbers (4 hours per night; 70% of nights over a consecutive 30-day period in the first 3 months) and is two criteria under an 'all'. The 'Documentation Required' sentences (re-evaluation within the first 3 months and not before day 31; documentation of both improvements in subjective symptoms and objective adherence data; adherence from device download / data card / usage inspection in a written report) are included as leaves of this pathway. 'Objective data related to adherence to PAP therapy' is represented by the adherence and download leaves rather than a separate criterion. The initial-coverage criteria are not re-nested in the continued pathway: the phases are separate pathways.

Continued coverage for non-OSA bi-level (E0470 and E0471): a signed and dated practitioner statement no sooner than 61 days after initiation, declaring compliant use (average 4 hours per 24 hours) and benefit; three criteria. The device-download sentence and the OSA re-evaluation sentences are not applied here because they speak of OSA symptoms and PAP adherence data; the document asks only for the practitioner statement.

Replacement: prescription + (nonfunctioning and out of warranty OR greater than five years old). The NOTE that physician attestation of OSA or essential sleep apnea 'will be accepted' when a previous diagnostic test is not available is modeled as an 'any' of the diagnostic sleep test criterion and the attestation, per the brief's rule for waiving NOTEs.

Accessories: one leaf, 'the coverage criteria for the PAP device are met', answerable because a chart shows an authorized/covered device in use. The usual-maximum quantity table limits quantity, not coverage, and is recorded in the pathway notes. The humidifier sentence holds two requirements (ordered by the treating physician; for use with a covered PAP device) and is two criteria.

Left out as not requirements: the Description section (including 'Treatment of OSA is primarily based on all of the following' and 'Any score ... over 5 may mean'), the titration NOTE under restrictive thoracic and CSA ('Most titrations are started with Bi-level without a backup rate'), the ventilator cross-reference, the LOINC tables, the Reimbursement rules (rental for 3 months, purchase after compliance, most cost-effective equipment, maintenance in rental, stop billing on discontinuation), the general 'Documentation Required' list and 'An order for each item billed must be signed and dated by the treating physician' (documentation an order carries, not a chart requirement of a pathway), and the Definitions section (e.g. Excessive daytime sleepiness = Epworth >= 10, which informs the symptomatic-OSA question but is not itself a criterion).

Exclusions kept to statements of non-coverage/investigational status. The two E0471 life-support and OSA statements carry no code (E0471 is covered elsewhere); EPAP/OPT -> A7049, A7047, E0600, A7002; positional electrical devices -> E0530; duplicate/travel PAP, technology upgrade and PAP cleaning machines have no code in the table.
plan_types: All lines of business unless otherwise noted in the Program Exceptions section
excluded_plans: Federal Employee Program (FEP): follow FEP guidelines
State Account Organization (SAO): follow SAO guidelines

Medicare Advantage products: NCD 240.4 Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) Therapy for Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA); DMERC LCD L33718 Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea; DMERC LCD L33800 Respiratory Assist Devices

exclusions.text: Bi-level therapy with a backup rate feature (E0471) does not meet the definition of medical necessity for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.
Bi-level therapy with a backup rate feature (E0471) is considered experimental or investigational when used as a life-support ventilator.

Nasal expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) devices (e.g., Provent® Professional Sleep Apnea Therapy) and oral pressure therapy devices (e.g., ApniCure’s Win-x™ Sleep Therapy System) are considered experimental or investigational.
Electrical devices for positional obstructive sleep apnea (e.g. Night Shift™ Sleep Positioner, NightBalance®) are considered experimental or investigational.

Adaptive Servo-Ventilation, auto SV/BiPAP and auto SV advanced devices (E0471) should not be used in individuals with symptomatic chronic congestive heart failure (CHF) with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF less than or equal to 45%).
Duplicate equipment is considered a convenience (e.g., travel PAP) and does not meet the definition of medical necessity.
Replacement of a PAP device for the purposes of upgrading technology does not meet the definition of medical necessity.
PAP Cleaning Machines or devices are considered to be items of convenience and do not meet the definition of medical necessity.

Bi-level therapy devices with a backup rate feature (E0471) do not meet the definition of medical necessity when billed with any of the below listed ICD-10 diagnosis codes for obstructive sleep apnea.

Oral pressure therapy devices (e.g., Winx Sleep Therapy System) are considered experimental or investigational, but may sometimes be reported using E0600 (respiratory suction pump, home model, portable or stationary, electric) and A7002 (tubing, used with suction pump, each).
